//: LibreLane configuration. Base: the Tiny Tapeout CMOS5L template (Apache-2.0). Changes from the template are marked with a //<name> comment key next to them. See NOTICE.md for the origin of the memory-block settings.
//meta: Adds one step after the power-grid generator: it runs the tile's Metal4 power stripes across the memory blocks so they are powered. The step is in librelane_plugin_jsasic_pdn.py and odb_stripes.py at the repository root.
//synth: Synthesis recipe. The first four-engine run used DELAY 4 (not set here, so the flow's own default) and got 0.497 mm2 of cells including 9,559 buffers; AREA 0 gives 0.41 mm2 with almost none, and the tile has too little routing room for the larger netlist (three routing layers, of which only Metal3 runs left to right).
//routability: On. Global placement inflates cells where it predicts routing congestion. It made detailed placement fail on the first four-engine design, which was larger; on the present one it completes, and after six routing passes the violation count was 5,849 against 20,278 without it.
//drt: Increased to 25 after 16 runs ended at 380 violations and falling.
//grt: Global routing reduces each layer's capacity by 20% (the flow's default is 30%). At 30% the global router saw overflow that did not really exist and pushed seven wires across the 512-word block, leaving about 150 violations there that no number of passes could remove (first run with the swapped blocks). At 15% nothing crossed a block, but routability-driven placement, which uses the same setting, spread the cells less and the detailed router was left with about 400 violations in one dense area below engine 0's block (second run). 20% is between the two; tested locally to global routing it gave a Metal3 overflow of 51 and nothing across the blocks.
//clock: 16.66 ns = 60 MHz, the project's target clock.
//pdn: Power stripes matched to the memory block's supply columns (11.24 um pitch, VDD and VSS 5.62 um apart). Width 2.1 + spacing 3.52 = 5.62; pitch 44.96 = 4 x 11.24; offset 6.15 puts the first VPWR stripe centre at x = 9.03, which is the first supply column of a block placed at x = 3.36 (or 3.36 plus a whole number of pitches). Template values were pitch 50.0, width 2.1.
//pdn_cfg: LibreLane's power-grid script without its per-block grid, which has no shapes on a single-layer grid and makes the generator fail. The blocks get their power from Project.ExtendPowerStripes instead.
//stripes: Only the tile grid's own stripe pairs are extended across the memory blocks; no extra pairs are added over the bit-cell arrays. This halves the Metal4 taken by power around the blocks (19.4% to 12.5% of the layer in a trial) and leaves more Metal4 and Metal2 for signals.
//defines: PE_USE_LIB_CELLS makes pe_clkgate (src/pe_fifo.sv) use the library's clock-gate cell sg13cmos5l_lgcp_1 instead of its simulation description. The FIFO and data-memory bytes are latches written through these gates.
//halo: Keeps standard cells away from the memory blocks' edges.
//vhalo: 10 um of rows are left without cells along the top and bottom edges of each memory block (was 0.48). The blocks' pins are on those edges. In the run of 17 Nov at a 20% capacity reduction, the 92 violations left were in one area starting at the pin edge of engine 0's block (x = 630 to 720 um, y = 430 to 590 um), including the only LVS error: a short between two neighbouring pins of that block, A_DIN[31] and A_BIST_DIN[31]. Tested locally to global routing: overflow 58 against 51, nothing across the blocks, total wire length 1% lower.
//drc: Magic reads the memory blocks from their abstract and reports the power stripes crossing them as overlaps. DRC is done by KLayout with the CMOS5L deck instead, which sees the real layout.
//macros: Four IHP single-port memory blocks, one per engine: three of 256 x 32 (416.64 x 118.78 um) and, for engine 2, one of 512 x 32 (416.64 x 191.34 um; same width and the same power columns). Two sit on the bottom edge (orientation FS, pin edge on top) and two on the top edge (orientation N, pin edge at the bottom), so every pin edge faces the logic. The large block is in the bottom-left corner and engine 0's block is at the top from x = 273.12, which leaves the tile's own pins (top edge, x = 30 to 191) clear. Until 16 Nov 2026 these two were the other way round: the large block at the top took 191 um of the tile's height in the busiest part of the design, the global router pushed wires across it, and 2,215 of the 5,849 violations left after six routing passes were on top of it (docs/decisions.md). Every x is 3.36 + 134.88 * k: 134.88 um is 3 power-stripe pitches (44.96) and 281 routing tracks (0.48), so each block sits on the stripes and on the routing grid exactly as the block at x = 3.36 did in the probe build. Every y is a multiple of the row height (3.78). Corner names are LibreLane's; the blocks' fast corner was characterized at -55 C.
//pdn_connect: Tells the power-grid tools that each block's VDD!, VDDARRAY! and VSS! pins are the tile's VPWR and VGND.
//obstructions: No signal routing across the memory blocks on any routing layer (the tile routes on Metal2 to Metal4 only). One rectangle per block and layer, equal to the block's footprint.
